In the inaugural 2008 Indian Premier League season, Royal Challengers Bangalore, then owned by Vijay Mallya, acquired Kohli for $50,000 following his performances in the Under-19 World Cup.[77] Kohli managed one run in the opening match against Kolkata Knight Riders and initially struggled in the middle order.[78] A brief promotion to the top order in a match against the Deccan Chargers offered a glimpse of form,[79] but he soon returned to his original position.[80] He concluded the season with 165 runs, as Bangalore finished seventh in the league standings.[81] In the 2009 season, Kohli began with a series of low scores but found form with a half-century in the third match.[82] Despite limited opportunities, he made crucial contributions, notably in the semi-final victory over Chennai Super Kings.[83] However, he was dismissed for 7 in the final, as Bangalore lost to Deccan Chargers by eight runs, finishing as runners-up.[84]

The 2010 season saw Kohli elevated to the role of vice-captain. He emerged as a reliable middle-order batter and an athletic fielder,[85] with a notable 58 against the Deccan Chargers.[86] Bangalore reached the playoffs but were eliminated by Mumbai Indians in the semi-final, where Kohli was again dismissed for 7.[87] In the 2010 Champions League T20, he delivered key performances, scoring 47 and 49* to help Bangalore reach the semi-finals before falling to Chennai.[88][89] Ahead of the 2011 season, Kohli was the sole player retained by Bangalore for $1.8 million.[90] After a steady start, he hit peak form with a string of impactful innings, including a half-century and consecutive Player of the Match awards.[91] He also stepped in as captain during Daniel Vettori's absence and earned praise for his leadership.[92] Bangalore topped the league table and advanced to the final, where Kohli contributed 35 runs in a losing cause.[93] He concluded the season with 557 runs, finishing as the second-highest run-scorer.[94] In the 2012 IPL season, Kohli experienced an inconsistent run,[95] beginning with low scores before registering a few significant innings,[96] including an unbeaten 73 against Delhi Daredevils as part of a then-record 203-run partnership with Gayle.[97] Midway through the season, he assumed captaincy from Vettori[98] but could not guide Bangalore into the playoffs, with the team falling short in their final league match.[99] Kohli ended the campaign with 364 runs and expressed dissatisfaction with his performance, acknowledging the need for improvement.[100] Promoted to full-time captain from the 2013 season,[101] Kohli began with an unbeaten 93 and successive half-centuries,[102][103] briefly taking his team to the top of the table. However, a mid-season slump, coupled with inconsistent bowling performances,[104] derailed their campaign. Despite Kohli's individual scores, including a 99-run innings,[105] Bangalore failed to qualify for the playoffs. Retained for ₹12.5 crore ahead of the 2014 season,[106] Kohli endured one of his most challenging campaigns. Although he began with an unbeaten 49,[107] his form deteriorated with a series of low scores and multiple ducks.[108] Attempts to revive his form by opening the innings proved ineffective, and he registered only a single half-century in his twelfth match. With Bangalore heavily dependent on Kohli and Gayle, the team lost six of their first nine matches and was eventually eliminated from playoff contention.[109] Kohli ended the season with a 73 against Chennai.[110]

In the 2015 season, Kohli opened the batting for Bangalore alongside Gayle and maintained consistent returns, scoring 505 runs in 16 matches at an average of 45.90.[111] His notable performances included an 82-run innings as part of a then-record 215-run partnership with AB de Villiers against Mumbai,[112] and an unbeaten 44 in a rain-shortened fixture against Hyderabad.[113] Under Kohli's captaincy, Bangalore reached the playoffs but were eliminated in Qualifier 2 by Chennai. The 2016 season marked a significant phase in Kohli's career. He began with a series of half-centuries[114] and registered his maiden T20 century against Gujarat.[115] Despite a slow start to the campaign, Bangalore staged a strong recovery, with Kohli scoring four centuries over the course of the tournament.[116] He finished the season with a record 973 runs at an average of 81.08, claiming both the Orange Cap and the Most Valuable Player award.[117] Bangalore reached the final but lost to Hyderabad by 8 runs.[118]

At the onset of 2017 season, Kohli missed the opening three matches due to a shoulder injury[119] but returned with a 62-run innings against Mumbai.[120] Despite adding a few more half-centuries, Bangalore endured a difficult campaign, including being dismissed for league record of 49 against Kolkata. Kohli cited the team's lack of intent and conservative approach as key concerns.[121][122] Bangalore were eliminated early, finishing at the bottom of the table,[123] with Kohli scoring 308 runs in 10 innings.[124] That same year, he was named in ESPNcricinfo's all-time IPL XI as part of the league's tenth-anniversary recognitions.[125] Ahead of 2018, Kohli was retained for ₹17 crore, making him the most expensive player at the time.[126] He crossed the 500-run mark for a record fifth time and briefly held the Orange Cap,[127] but Bangalore failed to advance beyond the league stage. Heavy reliance on Kohli and de Villiers, alongside an underperforming bowling unit, contributed to their early exit.[128][129] The 2019 season began with Kohli moving down the order, a tactical change that did not yield the desired results.[130] He later returned to form with a century[131] and finished the season with a series of improved performances, but Bangalore had lost their first six matches and again failed to reach the playoffs.[132] Kohli acknowledged the late improvement[133] but pointed to ongoing issues in the middle order, leading to increased scrutiny over his long captaincy tenure.[134] Between 2020 and 2022, Kohli experienced mixed outcomes in the IPL. In the 2020 season, after a slow start, he delivered several steady innings that helped Bangalore qualify for the playoffs.[135][136] However, his conservative strike rate[137] and early dismissal in the eliminator contributed to the team's exit.[138] In 2021, he began positively and reached multiple individual milestones, including becoming the first player to play 200 matches for Bangalore[139] and surpassing 10,000 runs in T20 cricket.[140] Midway through the season, Kohli announced his decision to step down from captaincy at the end of the campaign.[141] Bangalore again reached the playoffs, but Kohli's dip in form coincided with the team's elimination.[142] In 2022, under new captain Faf du Plessis, Kohli faced a prolonged lean patch,[143] recording multiple low scores and three ducks, which is the joint-highest in a single season of his career.[144] His struggles drew criticism from analysts and led to suggestions of taking a break from cricket.[145] He responded with a 73-run innings in a must-win match that secured Bangalore a place in the playoffs,[146] but failed to make a significant impact in the knockout games. The season concluded without a title, extending championship drought.

In the inaugural match of 2023 season, Kohli began with an unbeaten 82 against Mumbai[147] and maintained steady form, registering five half-centuries in the first eight matches.[148] His approach combined early aggression in the powerplay with a more measured tempo through the middle overs.[149] He also briefly captained the team in Faf du Plessis's absence.[150] Despite ending the season with back-to-back centuries, surpassing Gayle's record for most IPL hundreds.[151][152] Bangalore failed to secure a playoff spot. Kohli concluded the campaign with 639 runs at an average of 53.2 and a strike rate of 140. Further in 2024, Kohli played in rhythm, scoring several fifties[153][154] and a career-best unbeaten 113 against Rajasthan, though it came in a defeat.[155] Bangalore recovered from a six-match losing streak with a six-match winning streak to enter the playoffs, with Kohli contributing significantly,[156] including a notable 92 off 47.[157] He ended the season with 741 runs at 61.75, earning the Orange Cap for the second time.[158] In the 2025 IPL season, Kohli scored 657 runs in 15 innings at an average of 54.75 and a strike rate of 146.5, finishing as the tournament's third-highest run-scorer. In the final against Punjab Kings, he contributed 43 runs off 35 balls as Bengaluru posted 190/9, eventually winning the match by six runs. The victory marked the franchise's first IPL title, ending an 18-year wait. It was also Kohli's first IPL championship in 18 seasons with the team.[159] In 2026, Kohli contributed in the back-to-back IPL title wins for Bengaluru, being the team's highest run scorer and Player of the Match of the finals.[160]

Player profile
Playing style

Kohli playing his famous flick shot at the 2015 Cricket World Cup
Kohli is considered as an enterprising batsman, possessing technical abilities and a dynamic playing demeanour.[161][162] His customarily batting position in ODl cricket is at number three, with a slightly open-chested stance, and a resolute grip on the bottom handle of his bat.[163] He has been noted for his agile footwork, expansive range of strokes, and his propensity for adeptly orchestrating innings whilst thriving in high-pressure situations.[164][165] In his batting technique, Kohli tends to favour playing grounded shots rather than attempting big hits. He is appreciated for his ability to execute wrist shots and his consistent prowess in the mid-wicket and cover region.[166][167] Kohli has often expressed his admiration for the cover drive, which he considers to be his signature stroke. He possesses a natural aptitude for the flick shot, particularly when facing deliveries aimed towards leg stump.[4] Having a limited recourse to the sweep shot, Kohli's batting technique is characterized by an emphasis on ground shots that primarily yield runs in the regions between deep square leg and mid-on.[168] Kohli is known for his composed batting technique and versatility in his play. He scores runs between long-off and long-on with an aligned bat, while also possessing the ability to display a destructive streak. His combination of bat-speed and supple wrist movements enable him to craft innovative angles that disrupt traditional field positioning.[169] Kohli is also a proficient fielder, recognized for his quick reflexes and sure-handedness.[170]

However, Kohli has a known vulnerability to deliveries that are wide of the off-stump.[171] Bowlers often exploit this weakness by targeting him with such deliveries, especially in Test and ODl matches.[172] This vulnerability has resulted in Kohli's dismissal on numerous occasions.[173][174] Former New Zealand cricketer Richard Hadlee has also noted that Kohli is particularly susceptible to out-swinging deliveries.[175]

Kohli has garnered widespread acclaim and recognition as a preeminent limited-overs batter by cricketing experts and aficionados alike.[176][177] In ODIs, he boasts an average of 65.5 runs when batting second and 51.7 runs when batting first.[178] He has amassed 28 of his 51 ODI hundreds in run-chases,[179] and holds the record for the most hundreds scored when batting second.[180] In reference to his success while batting second, Kohli has expressed a fondness for the challenge of chasing, relishing the opportunity to test himself and demonstrate his ability to efficiently manage strike rotation and execute boundary hits.[181] His colleagues admire his self-assurance, dedication, concentration, and work ethic, which are the driving forces behind his success.[182][183]

Aggression
Kohli's playing style is widely regarded as aggressive, a trait that extends to his leadership on the field. He is known for his passionate and animated responses to on-field situations, demonstrating a fierce competitiveness.[184][185] His captaincy is characterized as proactive, taking bold decisions and leading the team by example.[186] Kohli has been the subject of much media scrutiny and criticism in the early stages of his career. He was often portrayed as a brash and arrogant individual, eliciting mixed reactions from fans, critics and former cricketers alike.[187][188] While some have praised his assertiveness and confidence,[189][190] others have criticized Kohli's behaviour for crossing the boundaries of fair play and for losing control, sometimes resulting in a loss of composure.[191] Despite his efforts to curb his aggressive behaviour, Kohli has acknowledged that there are times when intense pressure or high-stakes situations may challenge his resolve. Nevertheless, the cricketer has persistently maintained that his aggression acts as a source of inspiration and drives his focus and motivation on the field.[192] Writing for The New York Times, Huw Richards noted Kohli's self-assuredness and "assertiveness" in contrast to some former Indian cricketers who he felt had exhibited an inclination towards excessive politeness and reticence, and that Kohli embodies his combative demeanour both on and off the cricket field.[193] In contrast, former India captain Kapil Dev suggested Kohli's aggression was fake, saying Rohit Sharma "doesn't show fake aggression like Kohli."[194]

Comparisons to Sachin Tendulkar
Kohli's batting style and approach to the game have frequently drawn comparisons to Sachin Tendulkar, who he regarded as the epitome of excellence in cricket. Dubbed as Tendulkar's "successor",[195][196] he is widely considered to have the potential to surpass his records in the future.[197] His reverence for Tendulkar as a role model, who he idolized in his formative years and sought to emulate, is well-documented.[198] Indian commentator Aakash Chopra has notes that Tendulkar possessed a broader array of shots.[199] However, English batting great Kevin Pietersen has termed Kohli superior due to his impressive records in run-chases.[200]

In a discourse with Bollywood actor Salman Khan, Tendulkar proclaimed that Kohli possesses the potential to surpass his record of 100 international centuries. Tendulkar also acknowledged Kohli's batting aptitudes and the steadfastness with which he has accumulated runs.[201] In 2013, Tendulkar retired from international cricket, Kohli, who played alongside Tendulkar in the team, honoured him by presenting him with a sacred thread that had been gifted to him by his late father. Tendulkar eventually returned the thread to him, imploring that it should remain in his possession.[202]

Public image and in media

Virat Kohli in an Audi Q7 commercial
In 2008, Kohli was approached by sports agent Bunty Sajdeh of Cornerstone Sport and Entertainment after his notable performance in the ICC Under-19 World Cup. Sajdeh was impressed with Kohli's leadership skills and attitude and saw great potential in the young cricketer. In 2013, it was reported that his endorsements were valued at over ₹100 crore (US$10 million).[204] Now in 2023, his brand value has reached ₹1,000 crore (US$100 million).[205] His bat deal with MRF is regarded as one of the most financially rewarding deals in cricket history.[206] In 2017, Kohli entered into a notable endorsement agreement with Puma that spanned over eight years and was estimated to be worth around ₹1.1 billion (US$11 million). This deal made Kohli the first Indian athlete to sign a brand endorsement contract valued at ₹100 crore (US$10 million) deal with a brand.[207] As of January 2023, Kohli is widely regarded as the most marketable cricketer, with annual earnings estimated at ₹165 crore (US$17 million).[208] Kohli is currently recognized as the most followed Asian individual on the social media platform Instagram, boasting over 274 million followers on the platform. Reports indicate that he is able to command a fee of ₹8.9 crore (equivalent to ₹10 crore or US$1.1 million in 2026) for each sponsored post on the platform.[209]

Kohli has gained international acclaim for his athletic achievements and widespread popularity, earning a prominent place among the world's most renowned athletes, as per ESPN.[210] In 2014, American Appraisal conducted an evaluation of Kohli's brand value and determined it to be $56.4 million, placing him fourth on the list of India's most valued celebrity brands.[211] The following two years saw Kohli's brand value soar higher. As per a report published in October 2016 by Duff & Phelps, Kohli's brand worth had increased to $92 million, second only to that of Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan.[212] In 2017, Kohli was recognized by Forbes as the seventh "Most Valuable Brand among Athletes", surpassing renowned sports figures such as Lionel Messi, Rory McIlroy, and Stephen Curry, with a brand estimation of $14.5 million.[213] By September of the same year, Kohli had amassed endorsement agreements with 17 distinct brands, and he announced that he would only endorse products that he personally uses and believes in.[214] The following year, he was featured on Time magazine's annual list of the 100 most influential people in the world.[215] In 2019, Kohli was the only cricketer included in Forbes' list of "World's 100 Highest-Paid Athletes". He was ranked 100th on the list, with earnings estimated at $25 million, with $21 million being procured through endorsements, and the remainder from salary and tournament winnings.[216] Furthermore, in March 2019, Kohli was named the brand ambassador of the mobile esports platform, Mobile Premier League.[217] Kohli's earning potential continued to climb, and in 2020, he attained the 66th spot in Forbes compilation of the top 100 highest-paid athletes in the world for the year 2020, with estimated earnings exceeding $26 million.[218] In April 2021, Vivo appointed Kohli as their brand ambassador ahead of the Indian Premier League.[219]

In 2012, Kohli was recognized as one of the best-dressed men by the fashion magazine GQ, appearing on their annual list alongside figures such as Barack Obama.[203] Six years later, in 2018, a documentary highlighting Kohli's cricketing career was released on National Geographic channel. The film aimed to celebrate his accomplishments in the sport.[220] The following year, on the eve of the 2019 Cricket World Cup a tribute was bestowed upon Kohli. Madame Tussauds renowned for their lifelike wax figures, unveiled an exquisite creation of Kohli in London.[221] Continuing the string of accolades, in 2019, on the eleventh anniversary of his international debut, Kohli was honoured with a stand named after him at the Feroz Shah Kotla Stadium in Delhi, making him the youngest cricketer to receive such a recognition.[222] In November of the same year, an Indian animated superhero television series entitled Super V premiered, featuring a fictionalized portrayal of Kohli's teenage years and his discovery of superpowers.[223]

Based on the provided documents, the novelty and key advancements of the **ContextRAG** project include:

* **Three-Way Retrieval via Knowledge Graph:** It extends standard retrieval by adding a knowledge graph of entities and relationships as a third retrieval source, combining it with dense semantic search and BM25 keyword search [1], [3].
* **Context-Aware Query Rewriting:** It leverages conversation history to rewrite follow-up questions into clear, stand-alone queries before retrieval, ensuring context is not lost during ongoing conversations [1], [3].
* **Multi-Source Evidence Fusion & Re-ranking:** It fuses evidence from all three retrieval mechanisms (semantic, keyword, and graph) and re-ranks the candidates using a cross-encoder to deliver a compact, highly relevant context to the LLM [1], [3].
* **Empirical Evaluation of Graph Retrieval:** The project systematically measures whether adding graph retrieval improves retrieval quality, answer quality, citation support, and latency compared to using dense, BM25, or hybrid retrieval alone [1], [3].

The purpose of the assignment is to **build a complete Employee & Task Management System using the MERN stack**.  
You must implement the UI shown in the design with React (any UI library) and create a Node.js + Express backend backed by MongoDB (Mongoose). The backend has to enforce all business rules (e.g., task assignment only to active employees, status‑flow constraints, capacity limits, overdue detection, etc.), expose CRUD APIs with pagination, a status‑update endpoint, dashboard and CSV‑export endpoints, and handle searching, filtering, sorting and proper error codes. The frontend must be responsive, validate fields, keep search/filters in the URL, and display server‑side validation messages [1][3].

**Features that must be implemented (as described in the assignment)**  

---  

### 1. Core Business‑Rule Enforcement (Back‑End)  
- **Departments** – only Development, Design, QA, HR, Sales are allowed.  
- **Task Assignment** – a task can be assigned only to an **Active** employee; assignment to an **Inactive** employee is always rejected; assignment to an **On‑Leave** employee is rejected when the task’s *Start Date* falls inside the leave period (inclusive).  
- **Date Validation** – *Due Date* cannot be earlier than *Start Date*.  
- **Status Flow** – allowed transitions:  
  - Todo → In Progress → Completed  
  - Todo / In Progress → Cancelled  
  Any other change must be rejected. New tasks start as **Todo** and status changes are performed only through `PUT /api/tasks/:id/status`.  
- **Edit Restrictions** – tasks whose status is **Completed** or **Cancelled** cannot be edited.  
- **Completed Date** – set automatically by the back‑end when a task becomes **Completed** (never supplied by the front‑end).  
- **Capacity Limit** – an employee may hold at most **3 active tasks** (Todo + In Progress) simultaneously.  
- **Overdue Detection** – a task is overdue when today > *Due Date* and status is not **Completed** or **Cancelled**; this flag must be shown consistently in lists, detail view, dashboard and CSV export.  
- **Employee Deletion** – forbidden while the employee has any Todo or In Progress tasks. After deletion, old tasks must still display meaningful employee information.  

*(Sources [1], [4], [5])*  

---  

### 2. Back‑End API Requirements  
- **CRUD APIs** for **Employees** and **Tasks** (Add, Edit, Delete, View) with **pagination**.  
- **Status‑Update API** (`PUT /api/tasks/:id/status`).  
- **Dashboard API** – returns counts and per‑employee workload, all calculated on the server.  
- **Export CSV API** – downloads all tasks that match the current server‑side filters (not only the visible page).  
- **Search / Filter / Sort** – server‑side handling of:  
  - Search by *task title* and *employee name*  
  - Filters: department, priority, status, due date  
  - Sorting: created date, due date, priority (by importance), title  
  - All filters can be combined.  
- **Error Handling** – proper HTTP status codes:  
  - `400` for invalid data or broken business rule  
  - `404` for not found  
  - `409` for duplicate employee ID or email.  

*(Sources [1], [4], [5])*  

---  

### 3. Front‑End Requirements  
- **Responsive UI** (mobile, tablet, desktop) built with **React** and any UI library.  
- **Field Validation** – same validation rules as the back‑end (e.g., required fields, email format, date rules).  
- **Routing** – separate routes/pages for **List**, **Add**, **Edit**, and **View** for both Employees and Tasks.  
- **Reusable Component Architecture** – UI broken into reusable components; consistent file structure.  
- **Status Dropdown** – shows only the **valid next statuses** for a task.  
- **Notifications & Loading States** – friendly error/success messages and loading indicators for all API calls.  
- **URL‑Based State** – search, filters, sorting, and page number are reflected in the URL query string (e.g., `/tasks?status=In%20Progress&priority=High&page=2`) so that refreshing or sharing the link reproduces the same view.  
- **Export CSV** – button that triggers the back‑end CSV endpoint, exporting **all** tasks that satisfy the current filters.  
- **Dashboard Page** – displays all numeric metrics returned by the back‑end dashboard API.  

*(Sources [1], [2], [3], [4], [5])*  

---  

### 4. Additional Deliverables / Quality Requirements  
- **No Authentication** – the application works without login.  
- **Deployment** – front‑end deployed on Netlify/Vercel/Render (or similar) and back‑end deployed separately; URLs must be provided.  
- **README & Documentation** – includes setup steps, environment variables, API overview, schema, employee‑to‑task relationship, handling of employee deletion, and answers to the specific questions listed in the assignment (e.g., where status transitions are validated, why Completed Date comes from the back‑end, etc.).  
- **Source Packaging** – provide a zip file (named `FirstName_LastName.zip`) or a Git repository.  
- **Code Quality** – avoid anti‑patterns such as inline styles, poor naming, hard‑coded mock data, fetching all records then filtering on the client, or storing secrets in the repo.  

*(Sources [2], [3])*  

---  

### 5. Summary Checklist  

| Area | Feature |
|------|---------|
| **Business Rules** | Department list, assignment restrictions, date validation, status flow, edit restrictions, auto‑set completed date, capacity limit, overdue flag, employee‑deletion guard |
| **Back‑End APIs** | CRUD with pagination, status‑update endpoint, dashboard endpoint, CSV export, combined search/filters/sort, proper HTTP error codes |
| **Front‑End UI** | Responsive design, field validation, multi‑page routing, reusable components, status‑only‑next dropdown, notifications, loading states, URL‑driven filters/pagination/sort, CSV export, dashboard view |
| **Deployment & Docs** | Deploy URLs, README with setup & Q&A, zip/Git delivery, .env example |
| **Quality Rules** | No auth, no hard‑coded data/secrets, server‑side filtering/pagination, clean code structure |

All of the above features are explicitly required in the provided assignment documents.

Masal AI : FDE Assignment (Round 2)
Build a small AI-powered web app that helps a real-estate salesperson prioritize inbound leads and act
on them. One required feature is entirely up to you to invent, and we'll dig into your decisions together
in a 30-minute interview.
Role Context & What We're Testing
You'd be sitting between our product and real customers, configuring, demoing, and troubleshooting AI
voice systems live, often on a call with someone non-technical. That means two things both have to be
true: you can build working software quickly, and you can explain what you built clearly enough that a
buyer trusts it.
This assignment tests both:
• Building — can you turn an ambiguous brief into a working product in a few hours, using an AI
model as a real product component rather than a demo gimmick.
• Explaining — in your README, your 3-minute demo, and a live 30-minute interview where you'll
walk us through your own code.
The Assignment
Scenario. A real-estate sales team receives hundreds of leads a day. A salesperson needs to quickly see
which leads matter, what the customer actually wants, and what to do next.
Core requirements (all required)
1. Lead intake — a form to enter Name, Location, Property requirement, Budget, Buying timeline,
and a free-text Customer message (e.g. an inquiry or chat transcript).
2. AI analysis — call an AI model to generate: Lead summary, Customer intent, Key requirements,
Objections/concerns, Recommended next action, and a Suggested response to the customer.
3. Conversational interface — the salesperson can ask follow-up questions about a lead ("what
should I emphasize on the call?", "make my reply more assertive") and get answers grounded in
that lead's context, not a generic chatbot.
4. Lead list & prioritization (required). Don't build only a single-lead form. Support multiple saved
leads , in-memory or a real database, your call , each showing its AI analysis, and rank or group
them by some notion of priority or quality your AI analysis produces (a lead score, a
hot/warm/cold tag, an urgency flag , you decide).
5. Clear display — a salesperson should be able to scan the AI output in seconds.
Your own feature (required — content is up to you)
Add at least one feature you believe would genuinely help a salesperson in this workflow. We're
intentionally not specifying it. Think about what happens before, during, and after this screen in a real
salesperson's day.

-- 1 of 2 --

Technical requirements
• At least one real AI API/model call , not a hardcoded or canned response.
• Deployed at a live URL we can open and test with no setup.
• A public GitHub repository.
• Free-tier resources only (Gemini API, Groq, OpenRouter, Hugging Face, Ollama locally, Vercel,
Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, or an equivalent).
• AI coding assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Copilot, etc.) are expected, but you must
understand and be able to explain every part of what you submit.
Submission Requirements
Submit all four:
1. GitHub repository (public), with a README covering: what you built, an architecture overview,
which AI model/API you used and how it's called, how to run it locally, key technical decisions,
known limitations.
2. Live URL we can open and test without setup.
3. Demo video, max 3 minutes, screen-recorded, showing: the product, the main workflow end to
end, your own added feature, and one interesting technical or product decision you'd want to
discuss. Loom, Google Drive, or an unlisted YouTube link all work.
4. AI usage disclosure — which AI tools you used and for what (e.g. "Claude for prompt design and
the initial React scaffold, Copilot for autocomplete, ChatGPT to debug a CORS issue").
How to submit: A google form link will be shared with you.make sure all live links shared on the form
are open for anyone with link.

with citations that show the sources.

hybrid retrieval (semantic search plus BM25 keyword search), an LLM-based answer generation layer,
authentication, multi-session chat, a React web interface and an admin console for monitoring, analytics and
system configuration.
The proposed ContextRAG goes one step further. It adds a knowledge graph of entities and relationships as a
third retrieval source, and uses conversation history to make follow-up questions clear before retrieval.
Evidence from semantic, keyword and graph retrieval is fused, re-ranked and passed to the LLM for a
grounded, traceable answer. The project will also measure whether the graph improves results.
2. Problem Statement
Language models can give fluent answers that are wrong, out of date or not linked to any source. RAG reduces
this by giving the model evidence from the organization's own documents, but many document question-
answering systems still have clear weaknesses:
• semantic search alone can miss exact terms such as codes, names and identifiers, while keyword search
alone misses meaning.
• neither captures how entities and facts are related across different chunks or documents, so
relationship-type questions are answered poorly.
• follow-up questions such as "What are its advantages?" lose their meaning when the earlier
conversation is ignored.
• splitting documents into chunks can lose useful surrounding context, and scanned files need OCR.
• answers are often shown without clear sources, making them hard to verify.
• an enterprise system also needs secure access, multiple user sessions, and tools to monitor and
configure the system.
The problem addressed by this project is how to build one practical, working platform that combines context-
aware query handling, three-way retrieval (semantic, keyword and graph), evidence fusion, re-ranking and
source-grounded generation, and then to measure whether the added graph retrieval gives better retrieval
and answer quality than dense, BM25 or hybrid retrieval alone.

accurate, grounded and traceable answers from enterprise documents. The specific objectives are:

1. Project Overview
ContextRAG (RAG Studio) is a context-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platform for enterprise

The current version includes document ingestion with OCR, chunking, embeddings, a Qdrant vector database,
hybrid retrieval (semantic search plus BM25 keyword search), an LLM-based answer generation layer,
authentication, multi-session chat, a React web interface and an admin console for monitoring, analytics and
system configuration.
The proposed ContextRAG goes one step further. It adds a knowledge graph of entities and relationships as a
third retrieval source, and uses conversation history to make follow-up questions clear before retrieval.
Evidence from semantic, keyword and graph retrieval is fused, re-ranked and passed to the LLM for a
grounded, traceable answer. The project will also measure whether the graph improves results.
2. Problem Statement
Language models can give fluent answers that are wrong, out of date or not linked to any source. RAG reduces
this by giving the model evidence from the organization's own documents, but many document question-
answering systems still have clear weaknesses:
• semantic search alone can miss exact terms such as codes, names and identifiers, while keyword search
alone misses meaning.
• neither captures how entities and facts are related across different chunks or documents, so
relationship-type questions are answered poorly.
• follow-up questions such as "What are its advantages?" lose their meaning when the earlier
conversation is ignored.
• splitting documents into chunks can lose useful surrounding context, and scanned files need OCR.
• answers are often shown without clear sources, making them hard to verify.
• an enterprise system also needs secure access, multiple user sessions, and tools to monitor and
configure the system.
The problem addressed by this project is how to build one practical, working platform that combines context-
aware query handling, three-way retrieval (semantic, keyword and graph), evidence fusion, re-ranking and
source-grounded generation, and then to measure whether the added graph retrieval gives better retrieval
and answer quality than dense, BM25 or hybrid retrieval alone.

accurate, grounded and traceable answers from enterprise documents. The specific objectives are:

• Build a knowledge graph of entities and relationships from the documents and add graph retrieval as a
third retrieval source (proposed).
• Fuse the evidence from all retrievers and re-rank it with a cross-encoder before sending a compact
context to the LLM.
• Generate answers grounded in the retrieved evidence, with citations and source traceability.
• Provide authentication, document management and multi-session chat.
• Provide an admin console for service monitoring, analytics and system configuration.
• Evaluate the system by comparing Dense, BM25, Hybrid and Hybrid + Graph retrieval on retrieval
quality, answer quality, citation support and latency (planned).
4. System Architecture
This is the current architecture and it is still progressing; it will be extended into the proposed architecture
described in Section 12.

15. Proposed Contribution / Novelty
The contribution of ContextRAG is at the level of the unified architecture. Dense retrieval, BM25, rank fusion,
reranking and knowledge graphs are established techniques; the project combines them in one working
enterprise application and tests whether graph-enhanced retrieval improves results.
• Context-aware retrieval: conversation history is used to rewrite follow-up questions before retrieval.
• Three-way retrieval: semantic, keyword and graph evidence are retrieved together for every question.
• Graph-enhanced context: entities and relationships add connections between facts that plain chunk
similarity can miss.
• Evidence fusion + reranking: results from all retrievers are merged and re-scored so the best evidence
reaches the LLM.
• Grounded and traceable generation: answers use only retrieved evidence and show their sources.
• Unified architecture: document processing, retrieval, generation, chat, authentication and an admin
console work as one system.
The benefit of the graph component will be claimed only after the evaluation in Section 16 shows it.

messages.content: What is RAG?

Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG) is an architectural pattern that improves the output of a Large Language Model (LLM) by first consulting an authoritative external knowledge base—outside the model’s original training data—before generating its response. This extra retrieval step helps reduce hallucinations and produce more accurate answers [1].

sources.text_snippet: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an architectural pattern that optimizes the output of a Large Language Model (LLM) by referencing an authoritative external knowledge base outside of its training data sources before generating a response. This reduces hallucinations.

Hybrid RAG combines dense vector representations (retrieving semantically similar items) with traditional BM25 keyword matching (relying on term frequencies). Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) combines these ranking scores to maximize precision.

details, dashboard and CSV.

meaningful employee details if the employee is later deleted.

CRUD APIs for Employees and Tasks (Add, Edit, Delete, View) with pagination.

date, priority by importance, title) done on the server; filters work together.
Return proper errors: 400 invalid data or broken rule, 404 not found, 409 duplicate employee ID or email.

Responsive design (Mobile / Tablet / Desktop).
Validate each field based on commonly used rules (frontend and backend).

Pages
Search, filters, sorting and page number must stay in the URL e.g.
/tasks?status=In%20Progress&priority=High&page=2. Refresh or opening the copied URL shows the same view.
Export CSV downloads all tasks matching the current filters (not only the visible page).

messages.content: give me all feature which is required to eomplent

**Features that must be implemented (as described in the assignment)**  

---  

### 1. Core Business‑Rule Enforcement (Back‑End)  
- **Departments** – only Development, Design, QA, HR, Sales are allowed.  
- **Task Assignment** – a task can be assigned only to an **Active** employee; assignment to an **Inactive** employee is always rejected; assignment to an **On‑Leave** employee is rejected when the task’s *Start Date* falls inside the leave period (inclusive).  
- **Date Validation** – *Due Date* cannot be earlier than *Start Date*.  
- **Status Flow** – allowed transitions:  
  - Todo → In Progress → Completed  
  - Todo / In Progress → Cancelled  
  Any other change must be rejected. New tasks start as **Todo** and status changes are performed only through `PUT /api/tasks/:id/status`.  
- **Edit Restrictions** – tasks whose status is **Completed** or **Cancelled** cannot be edited.  
- **Completed Date** – set automatically by the back‑end when a task becomes **Completed** (never supplied by the front‑end).  
- **Capacity Limit** – an employee may hold at most **3 active tasks** (Todo + In Progress) simultaneously.  
- **Overdue Detection** – a task is overdue when today > *Due Date* and status is not **Completed** or **Cancelled**; this flag must be shown consistently in lists, detail view, dashboard and CSV export.  
- **Employee Deletion** – forbidden while the employee has any Todo or In Progress tasks. After deletion, old tasks must still display meaningful employee information.  

*(Sources [1], [4], [5])*  

---  

### 2. Back‑End API Requirements  
- **CRUD APIs** for **Employees** and **Tasks** (Add, Edit, Delete, View) with **pagination**.  
- **Status‑Update API** (`PUT /api/tasks/:id/status`).  
- **Dashboard API** – returns counts and per‑employee workload, all calculated on the server.  
- **Export CSV API** – downloads all tasks that match the current server‑side filters (not only the visible page).  
- **Search / Filter / Sort** – server‑side handling of:  
  - Search by *task title* and *employee name*  
  - Filters: department, priority, status, due date  
  - Sorting: created date, due date, priority (by importance), title  
  - All filters can be combined.  
- **Error Handling** – proper HTTP status codes:  
  - `400` for invalid data or broken business rule  
  - `404` for not found  
  - `409` for duplicate employee ID or email.  

*(Sources [1], [4], [5])*  

---  

### 3. Front‑End Requirements  
- **Responsive UI** (mobile, tablet, desktop) built with **React** and any UI library.  
- **Field Validation** – same validation rules as the back‑end (e.g., required fields, email format, date rules).

- **Reusable Component Architecture** – UI broken into reusable components; consistent file structure.  
- **Status Dropdown** – shows only the **valid next statuses** for a task.

*(Sources [2], [3])*

messages.content: give me which api i used for this project

**APIs that must be implemented for the project (as defined in the assignment)** | Purpose | Typical endpoint (illustrative) | Notes | |---------|--------------------------------|-------| | **Employee CRUD** (create, read, update, delete) with pagination | `POST /api/employees` – add a new employee
`GET /api/employees?page=…&limit=…` – list / view employees
`PUT /api/employees/:id` – edit employee
`DELETE /api/employees/:id` – remove employee (blocked if the employee still has Todo / In‑Progress tasks) | All rules (unique employee‑ID, unique e‑mail, department list, status, leave dates, etc.) are validated on the back‑end. | | **Task CRUD** (create, read, update, delete) with pagination | `POST /api/tasks` – add a new task
`GET /api/tasks?page=…&limit=…&…` – list / view tasks (supports search, filters, sorting)
`PUT /api/tasks/:id` – edit task (only while status is **Todo** or **In Progress**)
`DELETE /api/tasks/:id` – delete task | Business rules such as assignment only to Active employees, date validation, capacity limit (max 3 active tasks per employee), and “overdue” detection are enforced on the server. | | **Task‑status update** (the only way to change status) | `PUT /api/tasks/:id/status` – change status according to the allowed flow (Todo → In Progress → Completed, or Todo / In Progress → Cancelled) | Completed Date is set by the backend when a task becomes **Completed**. | | **Dashboard data** | `GET /api/dashboard` – returns counts and employee‑workload statistics (e.g., total tasks, overdue tasks, tasks per employee) | All numbers are calculated on the server. | | **Export CSV** | `GET /api/tasks/export?...` – downloads a CSV file containing **all** tasks that match the current filters (not just the current page) | Filters, sorting, and pagination are applied on the server before generating the CSV. | | **Search / filter / sort** (handled on the server side) | Integrated into the `GET /api/tasks` (and `GET /api/employees` if needed) endpoint via query parameters such as `title`, `employeeName`, `department`, `priority`, `status`, `dueDate`, `sortBy`, etc. | Multiple filters can be combined; results are paginated. | These endpoints cover the required **CRUD APIs for Employees and Tasks**, the **status‑update API**, the **dashboard API**, and the **CSV‑export API**, together with server‑side **search, filtering, sorting, and pagination** as stipulated in the assignment documents【1†L1-L31】【4†L1-L22】.

messages.content: can you tell me the novelty from this pdf

**Novelty of the ContextRAG system**

1. **Three‑way retrieval** – In addition to the usual dense (semantic) search and BM25 keyword search, the platform adds a **knowledge‑graph retrieval layer** that extracts entities and relationships from the documents and uses them as a third source of evidence. This graph‑based retrieval is fused with the dense and BM25 results to improve answer quality [2][5].

2. **Conversation‑aware query processing** – The system combines the current user question with the full conversation history before retrieval, so follow‑up questions (“What are its advantages?”) are interpreted in context rather than as isolated queries [2].

3. **Evidence fusion and cross‑encoder re‑ranking** – Results from the three retrieval streams are merged (rank‑fusion) and then re‑scored by a cross‑encoder to keep only the most relevant chunks for the LLM. This tighter, more relevant context helps the generator produce grounded answers [5].

4. **Context‑aware chunking with metadata** – Documents are split into chunks that retain surrounding context (document, section, position) and metadata, which are then embedded and stored in Qdrant [2].

5. **Grounded answer generation with citations** – The LLM is forced to answer **only** from the supplied evidence, and each answer is returned with explicit citations to the source chunks, making the output verifiable [5].

6. **Built‑in monitoring and configurability** – An admin console lets operators tune models, chunking, Top‑K, retrieval strategy (semantic, BM25, hybrid), and safety toggles, and provides analytics on usage, latency, cache hit rates, etc. [3][4]

These features together constitute the core novelty of the project: a practical, enterprise‑grade RAG platform that combines semantic, keyword, and graph retrieval, leverages conversation history, and delivers traceable, evidence‑grounded answers.

ContextRAG
B.Tech Final Year Project — Progress Report
1. Project Overview
ContextRAG (RAG Studio) is a context-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platform for enterprise
knowledge. Users upload documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown or images) and ask questions in a chat. The
system finds the relevant parts of the documents and the language model answers only from that evidence,
with citations that show the sources.
The current version includes document ingestion with OCR, chunking, embeddings, a Qdrant vector database,
hybrid retrieval (semantic search plus BM25 keyword search), an LLM-based answer generation layer,
authentication, multi-session chat, a React web interface and an admin console for monitoring, analytics and
system configuration.
The proposed ContextRAG goes one step further. It adds a knowledge graph of entities and relationships as a
third retrieval source, and uses conversation history to make follow-up questions clear before retrieval.
Evidence from semantic, keyword and graph retrieval is fused, re-ranked and passed to the LLM for a
grounded, traceable answer. The project will also measure whether the graph improves results.
2. Problem Statement
Language models can give fluent answers that are wrong, out of date or not linked to any source. RAG reduces
this by giving the model evidence from the organization's own documents, but many document question-
answering systems still have clear weaknesses:
• semantic search alone can miss exact terms such as codes, names and identifiers, while keyword search
alone misses meaning.
• neither captures how entities and facts are related across different chunks or documents, so
relationship-type questions are answered poorly.
• follow-up questions such as "What are its advantages?" lose their meaning when the earlier
conversation is ignored.
• splitting documents into chunks can lose useful surrounding context, and scanned files need OCR.
• answers are often shown without clear sources, making them hard to verify.
• an enterprise system also needs secure access, multiple user sessions, and tools to monitor and
configure the system.
The problem addressed by this project is how to build one practical, working platform that combines context-
aware query handling, three-way retrieval (semantic, keyword and graph), evidence fusion, re-ranking and
source-grounded generation, and then to measure whether the added graph retrieval gives better retrieval
and answer quality than dense, BM25 or hybrid retrieval alone.
3. Project Objectives
The main objective is to build and evaluate a context-aware, graph-enhanced RAG platform that gives
accurate, grounded and traceable answers from enterprise documents. The specific objectives are:
• Build a practical document-based question-answering system using RAG that accepts common
document formats and supports OCR for image-based inputs.
• Split documents into context-aware chunks with metadata, create embeddings and store them in the
Qdrant vector database.

8.4 Context selection and reranking
The design takes a broad first-stage candidate set (Top-K is configurable in the admin console; the current
default is 10), re-ranks it with a cross-encoder and passes only the most relevant chunks to the LLM. A shorter,
more relevant context helps the model use the evidence better.
8.5 Grounded answer generation
Retrieved chunks are given to the LLM together with their source metadata, and the answer is returned with
source information so users can verify it.
8.6 Frontend
A React + Vite interface supports user login, document upload and chat, and talks to the backend through an
API client. The chat page has a New Chat button, searchable chat history, a paperclip button to attach
documents, a voice input button, a settings button and a Show Retrieval Diagnostics option; citations appear
below each answer.
8.7 Admin console
A System Administrator can open an admin console with seven tabs: Service Monitoring, Analytics Overview,
Users & Organization, Knowledge Base, System Config, Prompts Console and Observability Logs. Analytics
show usage figures and charts; System Config lets the administrator change models, chunking, Top-K,
temperature and switch features such as hybrid BM25 retrieval, cross-encoder re-ranking, query
expansion/rewrite and AI guardrails.
8.8 Search and vector sandbox
A search page lets users test retrieval directly: choose Semantic, BM25 or Hybrid (Reciprocal Rank Fusion),
select the distance metric (Cosine, Dot, L2), set a minimum similarity cutoff and number of results (K), and try
chunk segmentation on sample text. This helps tune and explain the retrieval behaviour.

8. Implementation Details
8.1 Backend and API layer
The FastAPI backend has separate routes for authentication, documents, chat and search. Configuration is
environment-driven. It connects the frontend, the stored metadata and the RAG services.
8.2 Document ingestion
Uploaded files are loaded according to their type; image-based documents go through OCR fallback. A
background ingestion task then performs chunking, embedding, vector storage, BM25 index update and
document-status update.
8.3 Retrieval
Retrieval is hybrid. Dense vector search in Qdrant finds text with similar meaning, while BM25 finds exact
terms such as identifiers, error codes and product names. The two result lists are merged with fusion logic to
give one candidate list.

13. Proposed Indexing Pipeline
Document → OCR / Parsing → Context-aware Chunking → Vector Index + BM25 Index + Knowledge Graph
• Parsing: Uploaded documents are loaded by type; scanned or image-based files go through OCR.
• Context-aware chunking: text is split into chunks that keep metadata and surrounding context
(document, section, position).
• Vector index: each chunk is embedded and stored in Qdrant for semantic search (implemented).
• BM25 index: each chunk is added to the keyword index for exact-term search (implemented).
• Knowledge graph: entities (people, systems, products, terms) and the relationships between them are
extracted from the chunks and stored, linked back to their source chunks (proposed).
14. Proposed Query Pipeline
Query + conversation history → 3-way retrieval → fusion → reranking → generation
• Query processing: the question and the session history are combined into a stand-alone retrieval query.
• Three-way retrieval: dense (Qdrant), BM25 and graph retrieval run on the same query.
• Fusion: the three ranked evidence lists are merged into one candidate list using rank fusion.
• Reranking: a cross-encoder re-scores the candidates and keeps only the most relevant ones.
• Context construction: the selected chunks (and related graph facts) are arranged into a compact
context.

ContextRAG
B.Tech Final Year Project — Progress Report
1. Project Overview
ContextRAG (RAG Studio) is a context-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platform for enterprise
knowledge. Users upload documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown or images) and ask questions in a chat. The
system finds the relevant parts of the documents and the language model answers only from that evidence,
with citations that show the sources.
The current version includes document ingestion with OCR, chunking, embeddings, a Qdrant vector database,
hybrid retrieval (semantic search plus BM25 keyword search), an LLM-based answer generation layer,
authentication, multi-session chat, a React web interface and an admin console for monitoring, analytics and
system configuration.
The proposed ContextRAG goes one step further. It adds a knowledge graph of entities and relationships as a
third retrieval source, and uses conversation history to make follow-up questions clear before retrieval.
Evidence from semantic, keyword and graph retrieval is fused, re-ranked and passed to the LLM for a
grounded, traceable answer. The project will also measure whether the graph improves results.
2. Problem Statement
Language models can give fluent answers that are wrong, out of date or not linked to any source. RAG reduces
this by giving the model evidence from the organization's own documents, but many document question-
answering systems still have clear weaknesses:
• semantic search alone can miss exact terms such as codes, names and identifiers, while keyword search
alone misses meaning.
• neither captures how entities and facts are related across different chunks or documents, so
relationship-type questions are answered poorly.
• follow-up questions such as "What are its advantages?" lose their meaning when the earlier
conversation is ignored.
• splitting documents into chunks can lose useful surrounding context, and scanned files need OCR.
• answers are often shown without clear sources, making them hard to verify.
• an enterprise system also needs secure access, multiple user sessions, and tools to monitor and
configure the system.
The problem addressed by this project is how to build one practical, working platform that combines context-
aware query handling, three-way retrieval (semantic, keyword and graph), evidence fusion, re-ranking and
source-grounded generation, and then to measure whether the added graph retrieval gives better retrieval
and answer quality than dense, BM25 or hybrid retrieval alone.
3. Project Objectives
The main objective is to build and evaluate a context-aware, graph-enhanced RAG platform that gives
accurate, grounded and traceable answers from enterprise documents. The specific objectives are:
• Build a practical document-based question-answering system using RAG that accepts common
document formats and supports OCR for image-based inputs.
• Split documents into context-aware chunks with metadata, create embeddings and store them in the
Qdrant vector database.

Uploaded files are loaded according to their type; image-based documents go through OCR fallback. A

Retrieval is hybrid. Dense vector search in Qdrant finds text with similar meaning, while BM25 finds exact

ContextRAG
B.Tech Final Year Project — Progress Report
1. Project Overview
ContextRAG (RAG Studio) is a context-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platform for enterprise
knowledge. Users upload documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown or images) and ask questions in a chat. The
system finds the relevant parts of the documents and the language model answers only from that evidence,
with citations that show the sources.
The current version includes document ingestion with OCR, chunking, embeddings, a Qdrant vector database,
hybrid retrieval (semantic search plus BM25 keyword search), an LLM-based answer generation layer,
authentication, multi-session chat, a React web interface and an admin console for monitoring, analytics and
system configuration.
The proposed ContextRAG goes one step further. It adds a knowledge graph of entities and relationships as a
third retrieval source, and uses conversation history to make follow-up questions clear before retrieval.
Evidence from semantic, keyword and graph retrieval is fused, re-ranked and passed to the LLM for a
grounded, traceable answer. The project will also measure whether the graph improves results.
2. Problem Statement
Language models can give fluent answers that are wrong, out of date or not linked to any source. RAG reduces
this by giving the model evidence from the organization's own documents, but many document question-
answering systems still have clear weaknesses:
• semantic search alone can miss exact terms such as codes, names and identifiers, while keyword search
alone misses meaning.
• neither captures how entities and facts are related across different chunks or documents, so
relationship-type questions are answered poorly.
• follow-up questions such as "What are its advantages?" lose their meaning when the earlier
conversation is ignored.
• splitting documents into chunks can lose useful surrounding context, and scanned files need OCR.
• answers are often shown without clear sources, making them hard to verify.
• an enterprise system also needs secure access, multiple user sessions, and tools to monitor and
configure the system.
The problem addressed by this project is how to build one practical, working platform that combines context-
aware query handling, three-way retrieval (semantic, keyword and graph), evidence fusion, re-ranking and
source-grounded generation, and then to measure whether the added graph retrieval gives better retrieval
and answer quality than dense, BM25 or hybrid retrieval alone.
3. Project Objectives
The main objective is to build and evaluate a context-aware, graph-enhanced RAG platform that gives
accurate, grounded and traceable answers from enterprise documents. The specific objectives are:
• Build a practical document-based question-answering system using RAG that accepts common
document formats and supports OCR for image-based inputs.
• Split documents into context-aware chunks with metadata, create embeddings and store them in the
Qdrant vector database.

4. System Architecture
This is the current architecture and it is still progressing; it will be extended into the proposed architecture

Figure 1. ContextRAG system architecture. Green = implemented; yellow with dashed border = designed, needs validation.
Default models shown in the admin console are Google text-embedding-004 (embeddings) and Gemini 3.5
Flash (LLM), both configurable. The design also uses a BGE cross-encoder for re-ranking. Detailed status of
each module is given in Section 6.

-- 2 of 12 --

8.4 Context selection and reranking
The design takes a broad first-stage candidate set (Top-K is configurable in the admin console; the current
default is 10), re-ranks it with a cross-encoder and passes only the most relevant chunks to the LLM. A shorter,
more relevant context helps the model use the evidence better.
8.5 Grounded answer generation
Retrieved chunks are given to the LLM together with their source metadata, and the answer is returned with
source information so users can verify it.
8.6 Frontend
A React + Vite interface supports user login, document upload and chat, and talks to the backend through an
API client. The chat page has a New Chat button, searchable chat history, a paperclip button to attach
documents, a voice input button, a settings button and a Show Retrieval Diagnostics option; citations appear
below each answer.
8.7 Admin console
A System Administrator can open an admin console with seven tabs: Service Monitoring, Analytics Overview,
Users & Organization, Knowledge Base, System Config, Prompts Console and Observability Logs. Analytics
show usage figures and charts; System Config lets the administrator change models, chunking, Top-K,
temperature and switch features such as hybrid BM25 retrieval, cross-encoder re-ranking, query
expansion/rewrite and AI guardrails.
8.8 Search and vector sandbox
A search page lets users test retrieval directly: choose Semantic, BM25 or Hybrid (Reciprocal Rank Fusion),
select the distance metric (Cosine, Dot, L2), set a minimum similarity cutoff and number of results (K), and try
chunk segmentation on sample text. This helps tune and explain the retrieval behaviour.

• Generation: the LLM answers only from this evidence and the answer is returned with citations and
sources.
15. Proposed Contribution / Novelty
The contribution of ContextRAG is at the level of the unified architecture. Dense retrieval, BM25, rank fusion,
reranking and knowledge graphs are established techniques; the project combines them in one working
enterprise application and tests whether graph-enhanced retrieval improves results.
• Context-aware retrieval: conversation history is used to rewrite follow-up questions before retrieval.
• Three-way retrieval: semantic, keyword and graph evidence are retrieved together for every question.
• Graph-enhanced context: entities and relationships add connections between facts that plain chunk
similarity can miss.
• Evidence fusion + reranking: results from all retrievers are merged and re-scored so the best evidence
reaches the LLM.
• Grounded and traceable generation: answers use only retrieved evidence and show their sources.
• Unified architecture: document processing, retrieval, generation, chat, authentication and an admin
console work as one system.
The benefit of the graph component will be claimed only after the evaluation in Section 16 shows it.
16. Evaluation Plan
A fixed set of questions with reference answers and known relevant source passages will be prepared from
representative documents (for example 50 to 100 questions, including relationship-type questions). The same
documents, LLM and settings will be used for every configuration so that results are comparable.

Rohit Gurunath Sharma (born 30 April 1987) is an Indian international cricketer and the former captain of the India national cricket team in all formats of the game.[3] He is a right-handed top-order batter. He represents Mumbai in domestic cricket and Mumbai Indians in the Indian Premier League. Sharma was a member of the teams that won the 2007 T20 World Cup, the 2013 ICC Champions Trophy and was the winning captain of the 2024 T20 World Cup and the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy. Sharma is widely regarded as a modern-day great, known for his leadership and explosive batting.[4]

Sharma joined a cricket camp in 1999 with his uncle's money. Dinesh Lad, his coach at the camp, asked him to change his school to Swami Vivekanand International School, where Lad was the coach and the cricket facilities were better than those at Sharma's old school. Sharma recollects, "I told him I couldn't afford it, but he got me a scholarship. So for four years I didn't pay a penny, and did well in my cricket".[16] Sharma started as an off-spinner who could bat a bit before Lad noticed his batting ability and promoted him from number eight to open the innings. He excelled in the Harris and Giles Shield school cricket tournaments, scoring a century on debut as an opener.[17]

Youth career
Sharma made his List A debut for West Zone against Central Zone in the Deodhar Trophy at Gwalior in March 2005. Batting at number eight, he scored 31 not out as West Zone won by 3 wickets with 24 balls remaining. Cheteshwar Pujara and Ravindra Jadeja made their debuts in the same match.[18] It was Sharma's unbeaten innings of 142 in 123 balls against North Zone at the Maharanna Bhupal College Ground in Udaipur in the same tournament that brought him into the limelight.[19] He visited Abu Dhabi and Australia with the India A squad and was then included among India's 30-member probable's list for the upcoming ICC Champions Trophy tournament, although he did not make the final squad.[20]

Sharma made his first-class debut for India A against New Zealand A at Darwin in July 2006. He scored 57 and 22 as India won by 3 wickets.[21] He made his Ranji Trophy debut for Mumbai in the 2006–07 season and scored 205 off 267 balls against Gujarat.[22] Mumbai went on to win the tournament with Sharma scoring a half-century (57) in his second innings in the final against Bengal.[23]

Sharma has spent his entire domestic first-class career at Mumbai. In December 2009, he made his highest career score of 309 not out in the Ranji Trophy against Gujarat.[24] In October 2013, upon the retirement of Ajit Agarkar, he was appointed team captain ahead of the 2013–14 season.[25]

Sharma joined a cricket camp in 1999 with his uncle's money. Dinesh Lad, his coach at the camp, asked him to change his school to Swami Vivekanand International School, where Lad was the coach and the cricket facilities were better than those at Sharma's old school. Sharma recollects, "I told him I couldn't afford it, but he got me a scholarship. So for four years I didn't pay a penny, and did well in my cricket".[16] Sharma started as an off-spinner who could bat a bit before Lad noticed his batting ability and promoted him from number eight to open the innings. He excelled in the Harris and Giles Shield school cricket tournaments, scoring a century on debut as an opener.[17]

Youth career
Sharma made his List A debut for West Zone against Central Zone in the Deodhar Trophy at Gwalior in March 2005. Batting at number eight, he scored 31 not out as West Zone won by 3 wickets with 24 balls remaining. Cheteshwar Pujara and Ravindra Jadeja made their debuts in the same match.[18] It was Sharma's unbeaten innings of 142 in 123 balls against North Zone at the Maharanna Bhupal College Ground in Udaipur in the same tournament that brought him into the limelight.[19] He visited Abu Dhabi and Australia with the India A squad and was then included among India's 30-member probable's list for the upcoming ICC Champions Trophy tournament, although he did not make the final squad.[20]

International career
Main article: Career of Virat Kohli
Kohli's international career began in August 2008 when the 19-year-old had a "surprise call-up" to the ODI squad for a tour of Sri Lanka.[35] He opened the batting due to injuries to senior players, scoring his first half-century in the fourth match.[36] After a brief stint with the India A team, he scored a century against a strong Australian bowling line-up in a tour match.[37] Despite an early BCCI contract, Kohli's place in the team was not secure. A turning point came in the 2009 Emerging Players Tournament in Australia, where he was the top run-scorer, leading his team to victory with a century in the final. This performance cemented his return to the national team.[38] He scored his maiden ODI century in December 2009 against Sri Lanka.[39] By early 2010, he became the third Indian to score two ODI centuries before turning 22.[40]

Virat Kohli (born 5 November 1988) is an Indian international cricketer and former all-format captain of the Indian national cricket team. He is a right-handed batter and an occasional right-arm medium-pace bowler. Considered one of the greatest batters in cricket, he has been acclaimed for his batting skills and records. Kohli has the most centuries in ODIs and the second-most centuries in international cricket with 86 tons across all formats. He is also the leading run-scorer in the Indian Premier League.

Kohli was the captain of the 2008 U19 World Cup winning team and was a crucial member of the Indian teams that won 2011 Cricket World Cup, 2013 Champions Trophy, 2024 T20 World Cup, and 2025 Champions Trophy. He plays for Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the Indian Premier League and for Delhi in domestic cricket. In 2013, Kohli was ranked number one in the ODI batting rankings. In 2015, he achieved the same in T20I cricket. In 2018, he was ranked number one in Test cricket, making him the only Indian to hold the top spot in all three formats. He is the first player to score 20,000 international runs in a decade. He was the Cricketer of the Decade for 2011 to 2020.

Early life
Kohli was born on 5 November 1988 in New Delhi into a Punjabi Hindu family. His mother Saroj Kohli is a homemaker while his father Prem Nath Kohli worked as a criminal lawyer. He has an elder brother Vikas and an elder sister Bhawna. His formative years were spent in Uttam Nagar. His early education was at Vishal Bharti Public School.[3] As per his family, Kohli exhibited an early affinity for cricket as a 3-year-old. He would pick up a bat and request his father to bowl to him.[4] In 1998, the West Delhi Cricket Academy was created. In May, his father arranged for him to meet Rajkumar Sharma.[5] Upon the suggestion of their neighbours, Kohli's father considered enrolling his son in a professional cricket academy, as they believed his ability merited more than gully cricket.[6]

Kohli fielding during a match in December 2010
In 2010, Kohli was appointed vice-captain for a tri-series in Zimbabwe and became the then fastest Indian to score 1,000 ODI runs. After a dip in form during the 2010 Asia Cup, he solidified his position with consistent performances, finishing as India's leading ODI run-scorer for the year.[41] Kohli played a crucial role in India's 2011 World Cup victory, scoring a century on his debut and a 35 in the final.[42][43] Further made his Test debut in June 2011 against the West Indies, but struggled initially and was dropped.[44] He was recalled and eventually found his footing, scoring his maiden Test century in Adelaide in January 2012.[45] On 28 February 2012, during the Commonwealth Bank tri-series in Hobart, Kohli scored an unbeaten 133 runs from 86 balls against Sri Lanka, helping India chase 321 in 36.4 overs to secure a bonus-point victory and remain in contention for the tournament final.[46] and a career-best 183 against Pakistan in the 2012 Asia Cup, being the standout performances.[47][48]

In May, his father arranged for him to meet Rajkumar Sharma.[5] Upon the suggestion of their neighbours, Kohli's father considered enrolling his son in a professional cricket academy, as they believed his ability merited more than gully cricket.[6]

sources.text_snippet:
Virat Kohli (born 5 November 1988) is an Indian international cricketer and former all-format captain of the Indian national cricket team. He is a right-handed batter and an occasional right-arm medium-pace bowler. Considered one of the greatest batters in cricket, he has been acclaimed for his batting skills and records. Kohli has the most centuries in ODIs and the second-most centuries in international cricket with 86 tons across all formats. He is also the leading run-scorer in the Indian Premier League.

Kohli was the captain of the 2008 U19 World Cup winning team and was a crucial member of the Indian teams that won 2011 Cricket World Cup, 2013 Champions Trophy, 2024 T20 World Cup, and 2025 Champions Trophy. He plays for Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the Indian Premier League and for Delhi in domestic cricket. In 2013, Kohli was ranked number one in the ODI batting rankings. In 2015, he achieved the same in T20I cricket. In 2018, he was ranked number one in Test cricket, making him the only Indian to hold the top spot in all three formats. He is the first player to score 20,000 international runs in a decade. He was the Cricketer of the Decade for 2011 to 2020.

Kohli's return to form began at the 2022 Asia Cup, where he scored his maiden T20I century, his first in any format in over 1,000 days.[70] He was the highest run-scorer at the 2022 T20 World Cup, playing an impactful innings of 82* against Pakistan.[71] His peak resurgence came at the 2023 World Cup on home soil where he was named the Player of the Tournament for scoring a record 765 runs in a single edition. During the tournament, he scored his 50th ODI hundred, surpassing Tendulkar's long-standing record.[72] In next year's T20 World Cup; Kohli had a lean tournament, however delivered a player of the match performance in the final, scoring 76 as India won the trophy. Following the victory, he announced his retirement from T20 Internationals.[73] In the 2025 Champions Trophy, Kohli was instrumental in India's victory, scoring a century and becoming the fastest to 14,000 ODI runs.[74] India later secured the title. On 12 May 2025, after poor Border-Gavaskar Trophy performances he announced that the Test-series would be his last, marking his retirement from Test cricket.[75]

Kohli at Greenfield Stadium during match with West Indies
Kohli's form in the lead-up to the World Cup was not at his best, however after a strong start to the 2015 World Cup with a century against Pakistan,[57] Kohli's tournament ended with a score of 1 in the semi-final loss to Australia.[58] A subsequent dip in form was followed by his first Test series win as captain in Sri Lanka.[59] From 2016 to 2018, he entered a peak phase of his career.[60] In 2016, he was the Player of the Tournament at the ICC World T20.[61] He became the first batsman to score double centuries in four consecutive Test series and was appointed captain for the 2017 Champions Trophy, where India finished as runners-up.[62][63] This period saw him break numerous records, including becoming the fastest to 8,000, 10,000, and 11,000 ODI runs.[64][65] In 2018, he became the No. 1 ranked Test batsman and led India to first-ever Test series victory in Australia.[66] By 2019, he became India's most successful Test captain, holding the ICC Test Mace for three consecutive years.[67] He scored his 70th international century in November 2019, but this was followed by a prolonged lean patch.[68] From 2020 to 2022, Kohli struggled for runs and stepped down from the T20I, ODI, and Test captaincy in succession.[69]

Kohli's return to form began at the 2022 Asia Cup, where he scored his maiden T20I century, his first in any format in over 1,000 days.[70] He was the highest run-scorer at the 2022 T20 World Cup, playing an impactful innings of 82* against Pakistan.[71] His peak resurgence came at the 2023 World Cup on home soil where he was named the Player of the Tournament for scoring a record 765 runs in a single edition. During the tournament, he scored his 50th ODI hundred, surpassing Tendulkar's long-standing record.[72] In next year's T20 World Cup; Kohli had a lean tournament, however delivered a player of the match performance in the final, scoring 76 as India won the trophy. Following the victory, he announced his retirement from T20 Internationals.[73] In the 2025 Champions Trophy, Kohli was instrumental in India's victory, scoring a century and becoming the fastest to 14,000 ODI runs.[74] India later secured the title. On 12 May 2025, after poor Border-Gavaskar Trophy performances he announced that the Test-series would be his last, marking his retirement from Test cricket.[75]

Kohli has won ten ICC Awards, making him the most awarded player in international cricket history. He won the ODI Player of the Year award four times, in 2012, 2017, 2018, and 2023. He won the Cricketer of the Year award on two occasions, in 2017 and 2018. In 2018, he became the first player to win all three major ICC awards including Cricketer of the Year, ODI Player of the Year and Test Player of the Year in the same year. He was honored with the Spirit of Cricket Award in 2019 and given the Cricketer of the Decade and ODI Cricketer of the Decade in 2020. Kohli was named the Wisden Leading Cricketer in the World for three consecutive years.

Kohli has won the most Player of the Series and second-most Player of the Match awards to his name in all three formats combined. He was honoured with the Arjuna Award in 2013, the Padma Shri in 2017, and India's highest sporting honour, the Khel Ratna Award, in 2018. Time included him on its 100 most influential people in the world list in 2018. Kohli has been deemed one of the most commercially valuable athletes, with estimated earnings of ₹634 crore (equivalent to ₹692 crore or US$72 million in 2026) in 2022.

After winning the 2024 T20 World Cup being named Player of the Match award in the final, Kohli announced his retirement from T20Is. On 12 May 2025, at the age of 36, he announced his retirement from the Test cricket. He is married to actress Anushka Sharma, and they have two children.
